INSERT INTO quiz_questions (moduleId, question, options, correctIndex, explanation, sortOrder) VALUES
(30005, 'What is the FIRST step in the systematic troubleshooting process when you arrive at a faulted machine?', '["Immediately check the motor with a multimeter", "Gather information: What is the symptom? When did it start? Is it consistent?", "Reset the fault and see if it comes back", "Replace the most likely failed component"]', 1, 'Gathering information before touching anything is the foundation of systematic troubleshooting. Understanding the symptom, timeline, and history guides your entire diagnostic approach.', 1),
(30005, 'A 3-phase motor measures 15A on Phase A, 15A on Phase B, and 0A on Phase C. What is the most likely cause?', '["Motor winding shorted on Phase C", "Mechanical overload on the motor", "Phase C fuse blown or contactor pole open (single-phasing)", "VFD output IGBT failure"]', 2, 'Zero current on one phase with normal current on the other two indicates single-phasing—the power path for that phase is open. Check the fuse and contactor pole for Phase C.', 2),
(30005, 'When using the half-split troubleshooting method on a circuit with 8 series components, what is the maximum number of measurements needed to isolate the fault?', '["8", "4", "3", "2"]', 2, 'Half-split divides the circuit in half with each measurement. 8 components to 4 to 2 to 1. Three measurements isolate the fault from 8 possible locations.', 3),
(30005, 'A VFD displays fault code F004 (Undervoltage). What should you measure FIRST?', '["Motor insulation resistance", "Output current to the motor", "Input voltage at the drive terminals (T1/R, T2/S, T3/T)", "DC bus capacitor voltage"]', 2, 'F004 indicates the DC bus voltage dropped below threshold. The first check is input voltage at the drive terminals to determine if the problem is upstream power supply.', 4),
(30005, 'A PLC output LED is ON but the field device (solenoid valve) is not energizing. What does this tell you?', '["The PLC program has a logic error", "The problem is between the output module terminal and the field device", "The output module is faulty", "The input sensor is failed"]', 1, 'If the PLC output LED is ON, the logic is correct and the module is commanding the output. The problem must be downstream: blown fuse on the output card, open wire, or failed field device.', 5),
(30005, 'Which cross-system fault pattern is MOST commonly missed by inexperienced technicians?', '["A blown motor fuse", "A safety circuit that is not satisfied, preventing all machine operation", "A tripped circuit breaker", "A failed proximity sensor"]', 1, 'Safety circuits sit at the top of the control hierarchy. If the safety system is not satisfied, nothing downstream will operate. Inexperienced technicians often troubleshoot downstream systems without checking safety first.', 6),
(30005, 'An intermittent fault occurs every afternoon around 2-3 PM and clears by the next morning. What is the most likely trigger?', '["Vibration from nearby equipment", "Thermal expansion from afternoon heat causing a loose connection to open", "EMI from welding operations", "Moisture accumulation"]', 1, 'A fault that correlates with afternoon heat and clears overnight is classic thermal behavior—a high-resistance connection that opens as it heats up from ambient temperature plus I-squared-R self-heating.', 7),
(30005, 'You are reading an electrical print and see that relay CR-5 has a cross-reference showing 15-3, 15-8, 22-1. What does this mean?', '["CR-5 has 3 coils on different pages", "CR-5 contacts appear on page 15 rungs 3 and 8, and page 22 rung 1", "CR-5 was replaced 3 times", "CR-5 requires 3 different voltages"]', 1, 'Cross-references on electrical prints show where a relay contacts are used. This tells you that CR-5 contacts appear on page 15 (rungs 3 and 8) and page 22 (rung 1).', 8),
(30005, 'After repairing a ground fault on a VFD output, what must you do BEFORE resetting the fault and restarting?', '["Increase the acceleration time", "Verify motor insulation resistance is acceptable (megohms to ground)", "Change the VFD parameters to reduce output voltage", "Replace the output fuses"]', 1, 'Before restarting after a ground fault repair, you must verify the insulation resistance is acceptable. Resetting into a remaining ground fault can destroy the drive output IGBTs.', 9),
(30005, 'What distinguishes an expert troubleshooter from a parts-swapper?', '["Experts have more tools", "Experts form a hypothesis BEFORE measuring, then take targeted measurements to confirm or deny it", "Experts work faster", "Experts always replace the cheapest component first"]', 1, 'Expert troubleshooters use the scientific method: observe symptoms, form a hypothesis about the cause, then take the ONE measurement that will confirm or deny that hypothesis.', 10);
